market_mood: Geopolitics and inflation dominate: Houthi drones hit Saudi Aramco's headquarters and Iran is stepping up attacks on shipping near Hormuz, while a hotter-than-expected September CPI pushed Treasury yields up and knocked tech lower.
self_check: My oil and energy calls have been by far my best (81% right) while pure geopolitics-and-defense calls are 0 for 5, so today I lean into the shipping/oil supply chain rather than defense primes. High-confidence calls have been only 50/50, so I reserved 'high' for the tanker idea where the cause and effect is most direct.

picks.reason: A container ship was sunk near Hormuz and Iran is shifting tactics to attack tankers, which drives war-risk premiums and tanker day-rates sharply higher.
With Iranian exports at zero and Gulf shipping under attack, refined-product cargoes travel longer routes at higher insurance cost, which lifts product tanker earnings.
September CPI accelerated with firmer core inflation and gasoline costs rising, pushing the 10-year yield up and reducing the odds of fast rate cuts.
The EU conditionally approved its $40B Kenvue purchase, clearing a major regulatory hurdle on a deal that has weighed on the stock since announcement.
Rising gasoline/crude prices and airport attacks disrupting airspace are a double hit to airline costs and travel demand, and AAL is the most leveraged major to fuel.
Cirrus Logic publicly confirmed it made bids for Synaptics, which often puts a company in play for other bidders even after the first pop.

Attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure and Hormuz shipping keep crude supply risk elevated, supporting oil majors.
Middle East escalation supports gold, but a hot CPI and higher real yields cut the other way.
Hotter September inflation pushed the 10-year yield up, which is a direct negative for long-dated Treasuries.

top_buys.pitch: Tanker owners get paid more every time the Gulf gets more dangerous.
top_buys.why: A container ship was sunk near the Strait of Hormuz and officials say Iran is deliberately stepping up attacks on shipping ahead of the US vote. When ships are hit, war-risk insurance premiums jump and owners demand far higher day-rates to sail the route, which flows straight into tanker company earnings. Iranian crude exports are at zero under the US blockade, lengthening voyages for replacement barrels. My tanker calls on similar news have worked repeatedly over the last two weeks.
top_buys.risks: A de-escalation or ceasefire would deflate rates quickly, and tanker stocks are volatile and already up on the first wave of this news.
top_buys.watch: Daily VLCC spot rate prints and any further attacks on vessels or Saudi energy facilities.

top_buys.pitch: Product tankers are the less-crowded way to play Gulf shipping disruption.
top_buys.why: With Iranian crude exports at zero and Gulf routes under attack, refined products must travel longer, costlier routes, which lifts product tanker rates. The market tends to focus on crude tankers first, so product carriers often re-rate a few days later. Energy was the best sector of the past week, so this call is swimming with the tide.
top_buys.risks: Product tanker rates are seasonal and can fade fast; a quick calming of Gulf tensions would hit the shares hard.
top_buys.watch: Clean tanker rate indices and insurance premium reports for the Gulf.

top_buys.pitch: Hot CPI plus a Middle East oil shock is a bad mix for long bonds.
top_buys.why: September consumer prices accelerated on costlier gasoline and core inflation came in firmer, pushing the 10-year yield up on the print. Rising oil prices from the Gulf attacks threaten to keep headline inflation elevated into the next readings. That combination makes aggressive Fed rate cuts less likely, which weighs on long-duration Treasuries.
top_buys.risks: A flight to safety from escalating war or weak jobs data could pull yields back down fast, lifting TLT.
top_buys.watch: Next Fed speakers and the following CPI/PCE releases, plus the 10-year yield level.

top_buys.pitch: EU clearance removes the biggest hurdle to its $40B Kenvue deal.
top_buys.why: The EU conditionally approved Kimberly-Clark's acquisition of Kenvue, a deal that sent KMB sharply lower when announced on fears it would never clear or would destroy value. With regulatory risk falling, attention shifts to cost savings and scale in a consumer staples sector that gained 3.7% last week. Deal-driven ideas have been my strongest category after energy.
top_buys.risks: Investors may still dislike the price paid, and remaining US regulatory or financing steps could drag on.
top_buys.watch: Remaining antitrust clearances and the expected closing timeline.

top_buys.pitch: Higher jet fuel and airport security scares squeeze the most fuel-sensitive US airline.
top_buys.why: Crude is firm after attacks on Saudi facilities and Gulf shipping, and CPI showed gasoline costs rising. Deadly attacks at Riyadh's airport are closing airspace and raising aviation security concerns, which is a headwind for international travel sentiment. American carries more debt and less cost cushion than peers, so fuel moves hit its earnings hardest.
top_buys.risks: Oil could retreat if tensions ease, and strong domestic bookings or a solid Q3 report could lift the whole group.
top_buys.watch: Jet fuel crack spreads and American's upcoming quarterly results and guidance.

summary.watch: Watch crude prices, any further Houthi strikes on Saudi energy or airports, and the 10-year Treasury yield's reaction to the CPI print.
